link: an unvalidated screen encodes weak proxies
evidence: A screen built without a [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) defaults to convenient proxies, and the convenient proxies are the least predictive: years of experience carries an [operational validity](#term:operational-validity) of .07 against .40 for [job knowledge](#term:job-knowledge-test) [1](#cite:1). Employers using exact-match criteria report rejecting qualified candidates outright (88 percent) [44](#cite:44). The [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) tie validity to important elements of job performance, which is what the job analysis supplies [32](#cite:32).

link: no validation evidence, no defence for an automated screen
evidence: An [algorithmic tool](#term:algorithmic-screening) used to make or inform decisions is a selection procedure under the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines), so the same validity evidence is expected of it [35](#cite:35); California treats anti-bias testing before and after adoption as a factor in the employer's defence [40](#cite:40). A firm that has not validated its criteria has nothing to show when the tool shows impact ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: judgement adds group difference without adding validity
evidence: [Unstructured interviews](#term:unstructured-interview) carry a [Black–White d](#term:subgroup-difference) of .32 at a validity of .19, against .23 and .42 for [structured interviews](#term:structured-interview) [1](#cite:1); replacing an informal screen with a standardised test did not reduce minority hiring at a national retailer, which the authors attribute to the informal screen being no less biased [11](#cite:11).

link: delay is itself a stage candidates leave at
evidence: Earlier post-interview offers were more often accepted [15](#cite:15); withdrawal from a multi-hurdle process tracked perceptions of the organisation and the process and differed by stage [16](#cite:16); perceptions of the process predict acceptance intentions [14](#cite:14). That slowness and burden compound is a [synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) of the three.

link: an anxiety-laden format is a reason to leave
evidence: Developers describe [technical interviews](#term:technical-interview) as time-consuming, anxiety-provoking and governed by unwritten norms [22](#cite:22); being watched halved performance and raised measured stress in a [randomised trial](#term:field-experiment) [21](#cite:21); face validity and perceived fairness predict attraction and acceptance intentions [14](#cite:14). The step from "aversive format" to "withdrawal" is a [synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker).

link: two filters that both miss capable people
evidence: A watched live-coding exercise screens on stress tolerance and format preparation [21](#cite:21) [22](#cite:22); an exact-match résumé screen discards candidates lacking a token [44](#cite:44). Applied in sequence, each removes people the other would have passed ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: questions that feel intrusive or exclusionary read as unfair
evidence: Procedural-justice perceptions predict organisational attractiveness and acceptance intentions [14](#cite:14); the inquiries the law reserves (disability, criminal history, citizenship) are the ones most likely to be read as intrusive [34](#cite:34) [47](#cite:47) [49](#cite:49) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: adds validity and the largest subgroup differences
evidence: [Work samples](#term:work-sample-test) (d .67) and [job-knowledge tests](#term:job-knowledge-test) (d .54) carry larger Black–White differences than [structured interviews](#term:structured-interview) (.23) while predicting at .33 and .40 [1](#cite:1); the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) require more validity evidence when a procedure is used to rank rather than pass/fail [32](#cite:32).

link: a wider pool means more people to assess
evidence: Affirmative filters admit candidates the negative filter would have removed [44](#cite:44); the assessment that follows has to carry the validity [1](#cite:1), and each added stage is a point of withdrawal [16](#cite:16) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: structure replaces impression with score
evidence: [Structured interviews](#term:structured-interview) predict at .42 against .19 for unstructured [1](#cite:1); the structure components that carry validity are used by interviewers who were formally trained [19](#cite:19).

link: the formula keeps the judgement from diluting the evidence
evidence: Formula combination of the same information predicts at r .44 against .28 for judgement [7](#cite:7); adding an [unstructured interview](#term:unstructured-interview) to test scores lowered accuracy and raised overconfidence [9](#cite:9).

link: validation evidence is the gate's currency
evidence: The [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) accept criterion-related, content or construct evidence tied to important elements of job performance [32](#cite:32) and expect selection-rate records by group [31](#cite:31); the SIOP Principles define professional practice [29](#cite:29).

link: faster offers, more acceptances, no quality penalty
evidence: Earlier offers were more likely to be accepted in both candidate pools, with no difference in performance or turnover between fast- and slow-offer hires [15](#cite:15).

link: candour thins the pipeline early
evidence: Realistic previews lower initial expectations and attrition during recruitment and reduce later turnover [12](#cite:12); some candidates leave because of the preview, which is the mechanism ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [12](#cite:12)).

link: moving the question moves the liability
evidence: [Disability-related questions](#term:pre-employment-inquiry) and medical exams become permissible after a conditional offer if asked of everyone in the job category [34](#cite:34); criminal-history inquiries for contract positions become permissible after a conditional offer [48](#cite:48); export screening separated from [Form I-9](#term:form-i-9) and postings written for all [U.S. persons](#term:us-person) avoid the 1324b violations DOJ has settled [51](#cite:51) [49](#cite:49).

link: the requirement in the ad becomes the filter in the screen
evidence: Roles that dropped [degree requirements](#term:degree-requirement) from their postings changed hiring by 3.5 percentage points and less than one hire in 700 economy-wide, because the screens did not change [68](#cite:68); employers report exact-match rejections of qualified candidates [44](#cite:44). The posting requirement is the screen's criterion ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a closed pool inside a thin one
evidence: No individual can initiate a [clearance](#term:security-clearance); only a [sponsoring](#term:clearance-sponsorship) agency can [80](#cite:80), so the [cleared pool](#term:cleared-population) within any local market is fixed in the short run. Small firms already report few or no qualified applicants at 87 percent [71](#cite:71).

link: segregated networks reach the same people
evidence: [Referral](#term:referral-hiring) networks are segregated and reproduce the founders' composition until cumulative hiring dilutes it [81](#cite:81); referrals are nonetheless the source with the best retention evidence [60](#cite:60), so a narrow network is both the best channel and the smallest ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a channel is not fixable until it is measured
evidence: Sources differ in tenure and performance [62](#cite:62); without per-source records of qualified rate, starts and retention the difference is invisible and spending stays on volume ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). The [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines)' selection-rate records are the natural place for the source field [31](#cite:31).

link: an unknown firm is judged on the posting alone
evidence: Organisation characteristics and image predict attraction [63](#cite:63) [64](#cite:64); where the firm has no footprint, the posting and the recruiter carry the whole impression ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: excluding by words and delivery shrinks a pool that was already small
evidence: [Masculine-coded wording](#term:gendered-wording) lowers women's appeal for the same job [77](#cite:77); cost-optimised delivery shows a neutral ad to fewer women [66](#cite:66); age terms and citizenship restrictions exclude by law [78](#cite:78) [49](#cite:49).

link: referrals reach people who were not looking
evidence: [Referred](#term:referral-hiring) applicants are more likely to be interviewed and hired and quit 10–30% less [60](#cite:60) [61](#cite:61); referral is the channel that reaches candidates outside the posting market ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: more referrals, same networks
evidence: A [referral program](#term:referral-hiring) draws on segregated networks and reproduces the founders' composition [81](#cite:81); referrals from below-median workers were worth less than non-referred hires [60](#cite:60).

link: remote work replaces relocation
evidence: 1.6 percent of job seekers relocated for a job in early 2023 [85](#cite:85); workers value a hybrid option at 8 percent of pay and half of surveyed firms use remote work to keep staff [70](#cite:70).

link: title and range set the applicant count
evidence: Within a job title, a 10 percent higher posted wage draws 7.7 percent more applicants [65](#cite:65); most competing postings show pay [75](#cite:75).

link: the words are the cheapest fix
evidence: Removing [masculine-coded words](#term:gendered-wording) restores women's appeal and belonging ratings [77](#cite:77); removing the listed age terms and citizenship restrictions removes the statutory violations [78](#cite:78) [51](#cite:51).

link: name the skills, drop the proxy
evidence: Years of experience predicts at .07 [1](#cite:1); non-degree hires made after requirement removals stayed longer [68](#cite:68); the [lever](#term:lever-record) works only with a changed screen [68](#cite:68) [44](#cite:44).

link: a source field makes the difference visible
evidence: Inside sources outperform outside ones on tenure and performance [62](#cite:62); the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) already expect selection-rate records at each stage [31](#cite:31).

link: a national pool with a program attached
evidence: 8.3 million veterans in the labour force, 41.8 percent of employed Gulf War-era II men in management and professional work [72](#cite:72); [SkillBridge](#term:skillbridge) supplies members in their last 180 days under a 75 percent offer standard [74](#cite:74); [VEVRAA listing](#term:vevraa) brings priority [referral](#term:referral-hiring) [73](#cite:73).

link: image forms through recruiters and word of mouth
evidence: Favourable images relate to better recruitment outcomes and are formed by recruiters and word of mouth [64](#cite:64); recruiter behaviour and process perceptions predict attraction [63](#cite:63).

link: see who the platform showed the ad to
evidence: A neutral ad reached fewer women through cost optimisation [66](#cite:66); targeted job ads are [automated-decision systems](#term:automated-employment-decision-tool) under California's regulations [40](#cite:40).

link: volume without fit overloads the screen
evidence: A posting that draws the wrong queue [65](#cite:65) feeds an exact-match screen that then rejects on tokens [44](#cite:44); the two compound ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: the rate ceiling sets the range ceiling
evidence: The labor-category rate contains the wage, [indirect costs](#term:overhead-rate) and profit [98](#cite:98) and moves only through the adjustment clause's limited windows [117](#cite:117), while market wages rose 3.1 percent in the year [103](#cite:103); a lagging rate is a lagging range ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a range the market rejects draws the wrong queue
evidence: Within a job title, a 10 percent higher posted wage draws 7.7 percent more applicants [65](#cite:65), so a range held down by the rate draws fewer and different applicants; most competing postings show pay [75](#cite:75).

link: an unaffordable range makes wider sourcing futile
evidence: Applicant counts respond to the posted wage within a title [65](#cite:65); a pool widened by remote work or [referrals](#term:referral-hiring) still prices the offer against the market ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [65](#cite:65) [70](#cite:70)). This is the matrix's A1→D1 dependency, now with evidence.

link: know the ceiling before recruiting
evidence: The rate is the contractual ceiling [98](#cite:98) [99](#cite:99); benchmarking against [OEWS](#term:oews) [110](#cite:110) and CALC+ [111](#cite:111) shows whether the range can compete; a pre-approved range lets the offer follow the interview fast, which raises acceptance [15](#cite:15).

link: a market-matched range lands above incumbents
evidence: External hires into comparable jobs started about 18 percent above internal promotees [93](#cite:93); incumbents below the new comparison point lose satisfaction and search more [92](#cite:92); the gap cannot be closed by cutting pay [112](#cite:112).

link: incumbent raises need rate relief too
evidence: Raising incumbents to the new hire's level is a recurring cost under a rate that moves only at adjustment windows [117](#cite:117) [98](#cite:98); the matrix's D4→D2 dependency, with the mechanism now cited ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a weaker package is easier to counter
evidence: Benefits are 30 percent of compensation [104](#cite:104) and arrangements are priced by workers at 8 to 20 percent of wages [115](#cite:115); 13 percent of [cleared professionals](#term:cleared-population) switched for pay in a year [89](#cite:89); a candidate comparing packages between acceptance and start has more to gain by withdrawing when the gap is wide ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: price the package the candidate is comparing
evidence: Working conditions are a central part of compensation [94](#cite:94); the WFH option is worth about 8 percent of wages and schedule predictability about 20 percent [115](#cite:115); benefits are 30 percent of cost [104](#cite:104) and the family premium about \$27,000 [105](#cite:105).

link: one sentence closes the negotiation gap
evidence: Stating that pay is negotiable removed the gender gap in who negotiates in a [field experiment](#term:field-experiment) with nearly 2,500 applicants [95](#cite:95); [posting laws](#term:pay-range-posting-law) raised wages 1.3 to 3.6 percent without reducing postings [97](#cite:97).

link: the posted range is the applicant-count lever
evidence: Within a title, a higher posted wage draws more applicants [65](#cite:65); disclosure rose 30 points under [posting laws](#term:pay-range-posting-law) [97](#cite:97).

link: see the compression before it happens
evidence: The [external premium](#term:external-hire-premium) and its performance cost are measurable before the offer [93](#cite:93); the [Equal Pay Act](#term:equal-pay-act) fixes the direction of any cure [112](#cite:112).

link: use the window, bring the evidence
evidence: The schedule clause allows three increases a period inside a window with a ten percent approval threshold [117](#cite:117); the [ECI](#term:employment-cost-index) and CALC+ supply the evidence [103](#cite:103) [111](#cite:111).

link: a lawful closer, unmeasured
evidence: Four in five organisations use [sign-on bonuses](#term:signing-bonus) and one in eight evaluates them [118](#cite:118); [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) on cost-type contracts only under a pre-existing plan [100](#cite:100). The link is practice, not evidence of effect ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a visible sign-on bonus is a relative-pay signal
evidence: Below-median earners who learn of peers'' pay lose satisfaction and search more [92](#cite:92); a [sign-on bonus](#term:signing-bonus) incumbents did not receive is such a signal ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: disclose, document, keep in touch
evidence: GAO requires notice of known unavailability and treats the proposal as unacceptable otherwise [108](#cite:108); declarations of availability have defeated dismissals [114](#cite:114); the COFC requires only a reasonable belief at submission absent a solicitation term [109](#cite:109).

link: a contingent start is a long wait
evidence: Earlier offers are accepted more often [15](#cite:15); a candidate held for an award date the firm does not control has every reason to keep looking ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [15](#cite:15) [108](#cite:108)).

link: speed is the one offer-stage lever with field evidence
evidence: Earlier post-interview offers were more often accepted with no later performance or turnover difference [15](#cite:15).

link: remove the anchor the law removed
evidence: Bans in about twenty states [106](#cite:106); the early bans raised the gender earnings ratio by about 1 percent [96](#cite:96); prior pay is no defence in the Ninth Circuit [116](#cite:116).

link: no request without a need; the clock starts at the request
evidence: A request needs access essential to a classified contract and a [facility clearance](#term:facility-clearance) behind it [119](#cite:119) [120](#cite:120); until it is submitted no investigation runs, and once it is the firm influences only the initiation phase [126](#cite:126).

link: a longer clock is a longer interval
evidence: The [clearance](#term:security-clearance) sets the [interval between acceptance and start](#term:offer-to-start-interval) at 197 to 243 days [126](#cite:126), and each additional week of that interval raised the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) by 22 percent in the one field study [144](#cite:144).

link: the wait is when the other offer arrives
evidence: Thirty-nine percent of hires who never started had taken another job and an external offer raised the odds of leaving (OR 1.18) [144](#cite:144); the offer-stage record carries the [counteroffer](#term:counteroffer) side [113](#cite:113).

link: paid work in the interval keeps the hire
evidence: Financial security lowered the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) (OR 0.86) and pay was the second reason given for leaving [144](#cite:144); whether paid [bridge work](#term:bridge-work) reproduces that effect has not been studied ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: bench payroll raises the rates that cap salaries
evidence: Labor not charged to a contract is an [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) allocated through the firm's pools [148](#cite:148), and the labor-category rate that caps the affordable salary already contains those indirect costs [98](#cite:98); a larger pool means less room in the rate ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: an interim starts the work before the final grant
evidence: [Temporary eligibility](#term:temporary-eligibility) may be granted where no adverse information appears, valid at its level for up to a year [119](#cite:119); no public figure says how often or how fast it is granted to contractor applicants [127](#cite:127).

link: a transferable eligibility skips the investigation
evidence: A current eligibility of equal or higher level is accepted without re-investigation absent an exception, with a determination due in five business days [122](#cite:122), against 197 to 243 days for a new industry case [126](#cite:126).

link: hiring only the already-cleared narrows the pool
evidence: The contractor and other [cleared population](#term:cleared-population) was about 1.35 million on the last public count and no one can start a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) alone [80](#cite:80); cleared pay carries a premium and 13 percent switched employers for pay in a year [89](#cite:89).

link: each extra access step extends the interval
evidence: The credential needs a [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship), a fingerprint check and a submitted investigation [138](#cite:138); the [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity) decision is due in five days but untracked [122](#cite:122) [145](#cite:145); the customer's own [onboarding](#term:onboarding) ran 41 days at one agency [125](#cite:125); every added week raises the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) [144](#cite:144).

link: named owners and early submissions shorten the steps
evidence: The credential request, fingerprints and investigation submission can precede the start [138](#cite:138); the [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity) request has a five-day standard to hold the agency to [122](#cite:122); the cyber certificate can be verified before day one [139](#cite:139); a named contact and a first-day plan are the practices the [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) study recommends [144](#cite:144).

link: fill the urgent opening from the eligible track
evidence: [Reciprocity](#term:reciprocity) runs on a five-business-day standard [122](#cite:122) and a new investigation on a 197-to-243-day average [126](#cite:126); separating the tracks lets the start date follow the clock each hire is on ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: shorter interval, kept contact
evidence: Each week of interval raised the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) by 22 percent and good company communication roughly halved them (OR 0.56) [144](#cite:144).

link: referred hires wait better
evidence: An employee [referral](#term:referral-hiring) more than halved the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) (OR 0.42) in the survey study [144](#cite:144); referral hires also quit 10 to 30 percent less across nine firms [60](#cite:60).

link: run the checks in the order the law sets
evidence: The [I-9](#term:form-i-9), [E-Verify](#term:e-verify) and [FCRA](#term:fair-credit-reporting-act) steps each have a trigger and a window [130](#cite:130) [128](#cite:128) [136](#cite:136); the export assessment is lawful only for controlled positions and apart from the I-9 [131](#cite:131).

link: the pool is U.S. persons, then cleared U.S. citizens
evidence: Controlled technical data cannot be released to a foreign person without an authorization [132](#cite:132); classified access for a non-citizen is a rare [Limited Access Authorization](#term:limited-access-authorization) [119](#cite:119); new petitions for workers abroad carry a contested \$100,000 payment [142](#cite:142) [143](#cite:143).

link: an award date is an interval the firm cannot shorten
evidence: A proposed key person is hired when the award arrives and must be reported if unavailable before it [108](#cite:108); the interval runs as long as the competition, and each week of it raises the odds the person is gone [144](#cite:144).

link: paperwork ahead of the start shortens the interval
evidence: Speeding [background checks](#term:consumer-report) and paperwork is among the [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) study's recommendations [144](#cite:144); the [I-9](#term:form-i-9) and [E-Verify](#term:e-verify) windows run from the first day, so what precedes it is the firm's to schedule [130](#cite:130) [128](#cite:128).

link: know the path before the posting promises one
evidence: The need, the minimum-number rule and the 45-day start rule are checkable before recruiting begins [119](#cite:119); the pre-award [sponsorship](#term:clearance-sponsorship) documents are listed by [DCSA](#term:dcsa) [146](#cite:146).

link: without an FCL there is no sponsorship at all
evidence: A firm cannot apply for its own [entity eligibility](#term:facility-clearance) and must be [sponsored](#term:clearance-sponsorship) on a real requirement with its key officials [cleared](#term:security-clearance) [120](#cite:120) [146](#cite:146).

link: unbillable waits raise the firm's rates
evidence: Unbillable payroll is pooled as [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) and recovered through the rates [148](#cite:148); the rate that caps the salary contains those costs [98](#cite:98); a small base spreads them thinly ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: the longer the clock, the larger the unbillable interval
evidence: The interval between acceptance and the first chargeable hour is the [clearance clock](#term:end-to-end-timeliness), 197 to 243 days [126](#cite:126), and every day of it is paid from the firm's indirect pools if the hire is on payroll [148](#cite:148).

link: poor adjustment lengthens the ramp
evidence: [Task mastery](#term:newcomer-adjustment) and role clarity, the adjustment [indicators](#term:indicator-record), correlate .38 and .23 with performance [152](#cite:152); the first-year output rise is steepest for those who learn fastest [157](#cite:157).

link: structured tactics and an insider predict adjustment
evidence: [Institutionalized tactics](#term:socialization-tactics) r .24–.40 and social tactics .29–.47 with adjustment [152](#cite:152); serial and investiture tactics roughly halved first-year turnover at one firm [155](#cite:155).

link: a referred hire arrives with an insider
evidence: Relationship building and insider support predict adjustment [152](#cite:152); [referred](#term:referral-hiring) workers quit 10 to 30 percent less across nine firms [60](#cite:60); that the referrer acts as the insider is [synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker).

link: no badge, no team, no early support
evidence: Early supervisor and coworker support predicts ninety-day outcomes and declines week by week [156](#cite:156); a hire kept off the site or the network by a pending credential misses those weeks [138](#cite:138) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: no senior time, no social tactics
evidence: The [social tactics](#term:socialization-tactics) that put insiders beside the [newcomer](#term:newcomer-adjustment) are the strongest [onboarding](#term:onboarding) predictors [152](#cite:152); learning from knowledgeable coworkers is 4 to 9 percent of compensation [158](#cite:158); without the senior's hours neither happens ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: budgeted hours make the capacity real
evidence: Job-related training cost is [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) in the rates [175](#cite:175) and accumulates in the indirect pools [148](#cite:148); the hours exist only if they are planned there ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: indirect mentoring hours raise the rates that cap pay
evidence: [Indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) is recovered through the rates [148](#cite:148) and the rate ceiling already contains it [98](#cite:98); more [mentoring](#term:mentoring) in the pools, less room in the rate ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a slot the junior cannot fill is no placement
evidence: Only qualified hours are paid [99](#cite:99) and unqualified billing was recovered on audit [173](#cite:173); a developmental hire without a category they meet has no contract to land on ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a category the junior meets, billed as such
evidence: The qualification rule is per category [98](#cite:98) [99](#cite:99); billing each person at the category they meet is what the audit found missing [173](#cite:173).

link: training that does not transfer does not shorten the ramp
evidence: Transfer depends on realistic practice, supervisor support (ρ .31), climate (.37) and opportunity to perform [162](#cite:162); the [ramp](#term:time-to-productivity) is the output curve the training is meant to steepen [157](#cite:157).

link: realistic tasks and an expectant supervisor
evidence: Realistic environments, behavioural modelling, error management, supervisor support and early opportunity to perform are the supported conditions [162](#cite:162); open skills need motivation and self-efficacy as well [163](#cite:163).

link: unmeasured, every departure is a loss
evidence: The federal cost-benefit study measured participants and society, not employers [171](#cite:171); without a cohort measure the firm cannot see the productivity–wage wedge it kept [159](#cite:159) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: sort for stayers; hold only what the law allows
evidence: [Four-fifths](#term:four-fifths-rule) of tuition reimbursement's retention effect came through sorting [160](#cite:160); repayment terms cut quitting about 15 percent in cited research [166](#cite:166) and are now barred or narrowed in California and Colorado [167](#cite:167) [168](#cite:168).

link: a repayment clause is itself an exposure
evidence: California AB 692 carries a \$5,000 penalty or actual damages per violation for contracts after January 1, 2026 [167](#cite:167); Colorado \$5,000 per worker and consumer-credit treatment [168](#cite:168).

link: a registered program is a placement with a credential
evidence: [Apprenticeship](#term:registered-apprenticeship) pairs paid work with instruction under registered standards [177](#cite:177); completers' earnings gains were \$240,037 [171](#cite:171); 42 percent complete within a year of the expected date [172](#cite:172).

link: mentoring is a program requirement
evidence: [Mentoring](#term:mentoring) is a component of a registered program and smaller employers told GAO the registration and reporting were especially hard [172](#cite:172); the hours come from billable seniors [99](#cite:99) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a named slot bounds the bet
evidence: Training for non-employees is [unallowable](#term:allowable-cost) [175](#cite:175), a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) cannot precede a need [119](#cite:119), and [SkillBridge](#term:skillbridge) owes offers to 75 percent of completers [74](#cite:74); naming the slot keeps the development inside those rules ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: measure cost against billed output over tenure
evidence: Output rises faster than pay through the first eighteen months [157](#cite:157) and training raises output twice as much as wages [159](#cite:159); the [apprenticeship](#term:registered-apprenticeship) study shows the cost-benefit method [171](#cite:171).

link: the wait can be the ramp
evidence: Payroll before access is [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) either way [148](#cite:148); spending it on representative training moves the output curve earlier [157](#cite:157) [162](#cite:162) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: milestones make the ramp visible and billable
evidence: [Task mastery](#term:newcomer-adjustment) correlates .38 with performance [152](#cite:152); the [ramp](#term:time-to-productivity) is measurable where output is counted [157](#cite:157); the category the person bills in changes only when the qualification line is met [99](#cite:99).

link: SkillBridge intake is an offer obligation
evidence: The partner commits to a minimum annual intake and to qualifying offers for 75 percent of completers [74](#cite:74); a firm without the slots to offer takes on an obligation it cannot meet ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: the ramp is paid at the finished rate or not billed
evidence: The rate assumes qualified productive hours [98](#cite:98); output in the first year runs below the finished level [157](#cite:157); the gap is margin or [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: onboarding starts before day one
evidence: A named contact, a pre-start check-in and a first-day plan are the practices the [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) study recommends [144](#cite:144); they are the first week of a structured program [152](#cite:152) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: each market-rate hire resets the comparison
evidence: External hires start about 18 percent above internal promotees [93](#cite:93); quits respond to comparisons with higher-paid peers [182](#cite:182); below-median earners who learn peer pay search [92](#cite:92).

link: similar raises across peers, reviewed at milestones
evidence: Separations were insensitive when raises were similar across peers [182](#cite:182); the [Equal Pay Act](#term:equal-pay-act) requires curing gaps upward [112](#cite:112).

link: retention raises meet the rate ceiling
evidence: The labor-category rate already contains wages, [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) and profit [98](#cite:98); a raise with no rate relief comes out of margin [117](#cite:117) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: portable skills are what the prime buys
evidence: [General training](#term:general-human-capital) raises outside value [161](#cite:161); external hires are paid an 18 percent premium [93](#cite:93); 13 percent of [cleared professionals](#term:cleared-population) switched for pay in a year [89](#cite:89).

link: the hold has to be in the job
evidence: [Embeddedness](#term:job-embeddedness) ρ −.26 [178](#cite:178); [firm-specific training](#term:specific-human-capital) −.40 with [unit turnover](#term:collective-turnover) [181](#cite:181); restrictions on the hiring party are criminal [187](#cite:187).

link: a collateral non-solicit, never a no-poach
evidence: [No-poach agreements](#term:no-poach-agreement) are illegal and criminally prosecutable; [non-solicit terms](#term:non-solicitation-agreement) collateral and reasonably necessary to a collaboration are judged on their effects [187](#cite:187).

link: strain erodes commitment and fit
evidence: Stress (.21), role conflict (.15) and work–life conflict (.19) predict quitting alongside commitment (−.29) and fit (−.29) [178](#cite:178); that the first erode the second is [synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker).

link: a 197-day backfill is a 197-day cover
evidence: Industry [clearances](#term:security-clearance) average 197 to 243 days [126](#cite:126); the vacancy is covered by the remaining staff for that long, with the strain the turnover evidence prices [178](#cite:178) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: scope or support instead of silent cover
evidence: The [key-personnel clause](#term:key-personnel-clause) already requires notice and a substitute [188](#cite:188); the strain predictors, not the hours, are what the cover raises [178](#cite:178).

link: the firm's own manager, regularly
evidence: Leadership ρ −.24, commitment −.29 [178](#cite:178); unit engagement relates to turnover across 7,939 units [183](#cite:183); supervisor undermining HR 3.01 [156](#cite:156).

link: onsite work draws only from commuting distance
evidence: Relocation is under two percent of job seekers [85](#cite:85); a 45-minute commute raised transfer probability ten points among teachers [194](#cite:194); the amenity the job cannot offer is worth about a fifth of pay [115](#cite:115).

link: what the contract allows, approved in writing
evidence: Workers price WFH at about 8 percent and schedule predictability at about 20 percent of wages [115](#cite:115); classified work stays at the facility [119](#cite:119).

link: a visible contract end sends people looking
evidence: [Withdrawal cognitions](#term:withdrawal-cognitions) (.56) and perceived alternatives (.23) are the strongest predictors of leaving [178](#cite:178); there is no [right of first refusal](#term:nondisplacement) with a successor [186](#cite:186).

link: known facts, dates, and no false promises
evidence: Perceived organizational honesty is the mechanism by which realistic previews lower turnover [13](#cite:13); the successor rule the firm might have pointed to is gone [186](#cite:186).

link: the step up is at the prime
evidence: Internal mobility is among the practices most tied to lower turnover (−.25) [181](#cite:181); where the firm has none, the larger employer's ladder and premium (18 percent) are the alternative [93](#cite:93) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: growth without the wrong promotion
evidence: Internal mobility ρ −.25 [181](#cite:181); promoting on individual output costs 7.5 percent of manager value added per doubling of prior sales, and teamwork experience predicts better managers [184](#cite:184) [185](#cite:185).

link: every move is a backfill
evidence: The vacancy left behind carries the posting-to-clearance sequence, 197 to 243 days where a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) is needed [126](#cite:126), and a named person's move needs the customer's consent [188](#cite:188).

link: the key person is the single holder
evidence: [Replacement costs](#term:replacement-cost) are largest for specialised skills in thin markets [193](#cite:193); a named key person's substitute must meet or exceed the requirement within the clause's notice [188](#cite:188).

link: a second holder and a named successor
evidence: [Firm-specific training](#term:specific-human-capital) is the practice most strongly tied to lower [unit turnover](#term:collective-turnover) (−.40) [181](#cite:181); succession metrics are part of the reporting standard [46](#cite:46); the clause requires a qualified substitute [188](#cite:188).

link: cross-training spends the senior's billable hours
evidence: The senior's hours are contract hours or [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) [99](#cite:99) [148](#cite:148); training cost is [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) in the rates [175](#cite:175) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: the clause, the report and the notification on day one
evidence: Thirty days'' notice and an [equal-or-better substitute](#term:key-personnel-substitution) [188](#cite:188); termination reported and adverse information reported after separation [189](#cite:189); agency notified where the person is in a live proposal [108](#cite:108).

link: an unavailable key person is a proposal problem
evidence: An offeror with actual knowledge that a proposed key person has become unavailable must notify the agency and the proposal is unacceptable otherwise [108](#cite:108).

link: the prime takes the single holder
evidence: The [external premium](#term:external-hire-premium) is paid for the trained person [93](#cite:93); the departure of a specialist raises the price of everyone adjacent and the cost of replacement most in thin markets [193](#cite:193).

link: attachment starts in the first ninety days
evidence: [Social acceptance](#term:newcomer-adjustment) → commitment .40 and [turnover intentions](#term:withdrawal-cognitions) −.27 [152](#cite:152); early support predicts commitment at ninety days [156](#cite:156); [investiture](#term:socialization-tactics) and serial tactics halved first-year turnover at one firm [155](#cite:155).

link: no contract, no sponsorship
evidence: Eligibility may be requested only where access is essential to a classified contract [119](#cite:119); an opening without a contract behind it cannot start the [clearance clock](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) at all ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a proposal opening is a contingent offer
evidence: A person named in a proposal is hired on award and must be reported if unavailable [108](#cite:108); naming someone the firm cannot deliver is a misrepresentation that can unwind the award [203](#cite:203).

link: funded, proposed or speculative, decided before posting
evidence: The [sponsorship](#term:clearance-sponsorship) need [119](#cite:119), the proposal representation standard [203](#cite:203) and the indirect-cost treatment of spend before funding [148](#cite:148) are each checkable before the posting ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: a blended requisition draws for neither job
evidence: The title and the pay figure set who applies, and titles differ in the pools they draw [65](#cite:65); a posting that names two jobs names neither ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: an untraced requirement is usually a degree or a years line
evidence: Roles dropping [degree requirements](#term:degree-requirement) rose fourfold while hiring without a degree barely moved because screens did not change [68](#cite:68); the category's own line is the enforceable one [99](#cite:99).

link: one scorecard, three sources of requirement, one example profile
evidence: The category line is what the audit validated by résumé [173](#cite:173) [99](#cite:99); structured, scored criteria predict performance [1](#cite:1) [7](#cite:7); the customer specifies the result, not the hire [197](#cite:197).

link: the category line is the customer's definition
evidence: Unqualified billing was recovered on audit [173](#cite:173); a candidate the firm calls qualified and the category does not is the junior in the senior slot [99](#cite:99).

link: the customer's review is part of the candidate's wait
evidence: Earlier offers are accepted more often [15](#cite:15) and withdrawal follows a badly perceived process [16](#cite:16); the review has no stated period in the clause carried [188](#cite:188).

link: agreed review days and an escalation name
evidence: The speed and withdrawal evidence [15](#cite:15) [16](#cite:16); the clause's silence on the government's period [188](#cite:188); the limit on customer direction that leaves the asking to the firm [197](#cite:197).

link: unpriced vacancies cannot be ranked
evidence: [Replacement cost](#term:replacement-cost) and unit-level effects are measurable [180](#cite:180) [181](#cite:181); without the estimate every opening carries the same weight ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: price the vacancy, not only the recruiting spend
evidence: The case-study median of about a fifth of salary [180](#cite:180), the unit-level [correlations](#term:correlation-coefficient) [181](#cite:181) and the unbilled hours [99](#cite:99) give the terms of the estimate.

link: a budget per role against the vacancy's cost
evidence: The [cost-per-hire](#term:cost-per-hire) medians and their components [196](#cite:196); bonuses [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) only under an established plan [100](#cite:100); the replacement-cost median as the comparison [180](#cite:180).

link: a cap on payroll carried before billing
evidence: The [30-day payment default](#term:prompt-payment) and the [15-day goal](#term:accelerated-payment) [202](#cite:202) [201](#cite:201); unbilled payroll in the indirect pools [148](#cite:148).

link: the cap limits the bench that bridges the clearance
evidence: A hire [sponsored](#term:clearance-sponsorship) for a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) waits 197 to 243 days on the firm's payroll [126](#cite:126) [148](#cite:148); a cap on carried payroll is a cap on how many can wait ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: the arithmetic decides before the offer
evidence: The [rate build-up](#term:wrap-rate) [206](#cite:206) and the fixed category rate [98](#cite:98) decide whether any salary the market accepts fits; the offer-stage [constraint](#term:constraint-record) is the same fact met later ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: loaded market pay against the ceiling, before posting
evidence: Market pay is public [110](#cite:110), the layers are stated [206](#cite:206), the ceilings are published [111](#cite:111) and the adjustment path is limited [117](#cite:117).

link: a standing start against a 197-day clock
evidence: Industry [clearances](#term:security-clearance) average 197 to 243 days [126](#cite:126); a firm that begins at the vacancy has spent none of that time ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); the planning principles ask for the gaps to be known in advance [205](#cite:205).

link: known openings, kept pipelines
evidence: The five planning principles [205](#cite:205); the [referral](#term:referral-hiring) and pipeline evidence that relationships kept before the opening yield hires [60](#cite:60) [74](#cite:74); the clocks the forecast buys time against [43](#cite:43) [126](#cite:126).

link: a forecast is not a funded opening
evidence: A cache of [cleared](#term:security-clearance) employees may not be built [119](#cite:119); a pipeline kept for a forecast opening is effort without a [requisition](#term:requisition) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: consent, inside the limit, without a no-poach
evidence: [Advance consent](#term:consent-to-subcontract) [199](#cite:199), the 50 percent services limit [198](#cite:198) and the antitrust line [187](#cite:187).

link: the partner's pool is capped too
evidence: Only half the amount paid on a [set-aside](#term:set-aside) services contract may go to non-similarly-situated [subcontractors](#term:subcontractor) [198](#cite:198); the gap the local pool cannot fill is only half fillable from outside it ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: without records the screen is never checked
evidence: Practitioners' beliefs diverge from the research most on selection [204](#cite:204); the [adverse-impact](#term:adverse-impact) computation needs the [applicant-flow records](#term:applicant-record-retention) [31](#cite:31).

link: a stage-and-reason record, reviewed against the evidence
evidence: The retention rules already require most of the record [200](#cite:200) [31](#cite:31) [40](#cite:40); the research–practice gap is largest where the record would show it [204](#cite:204).

link: unowned steps add weeks
evidence: Each week between acceptance and start raised [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) odds 22 percent [144](#cite:144); the steps are spread across the firm, the customer and the security office ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

link: one name, one calendar
evidence: Speed of offer raises acceptance [15](#cite:15), process perceptions drive withdrawal [16](#cite:16) and the interval drives [no-shows](#term:new-hire-no-show) [144](#cite:144); that an owner shortens them is [synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker).

link: late recruiting means long cover
evidence: A vacancy opened without a forecast is covered for the whole fill or [clearance clock](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) [43](#cite:43) [126](#cite:126); the cover shows as the strain that predicts quitting [178](#cite:178).
